basis: Thalamic neuronal injury defines disease; arrhythmias occur in 30-79%. Respiratory insufficiency does not establish direct lung damage.
Neurodevelopmental impairment with cerebellar atrophy; nystagmus and limited strabismus reports do not establish direct ocular injury. Asthma and reflux are separate diagnoses.
Intestinal fluke infection directly occupies the intestinal mucosa; ectopic infection is uncommon.
Site-variable myoepithelial neoplasm, most typically arising in salivary glands. Breast and soft-tissue examples do not establish additional organs across the umbrella.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes chronic airway disease; chronic middle-ear effusion and otitis affect >30% in primary ciliary dyskinesia. Situs inversus alone causes no damage.
Staphylococcal toxin-mediated infectious disease; the scarlatiniform rash is transient and does not establish lasting skin damage.
Progressive cerebral and cerebellar degeneration, seizures, microcephaly and profound developmental impairment define the syndrome.
Inherited disruption of thyroid hormone metabolism; no additional organ injury applies consistently across the umbrella.
Leukocyte aggregation causes microvascular obstruction; pulmonary dysfunction occurs in roughly 60-80% and neurologic dysfunction in about 30-50% of symptomatic cases.
Benign neoplasm located in the meninges of the central nervous system.
Childhood embryonal malignancy arising in the infratentorial brain.
Hereditary colorectal cancer syndrome; extracolonic cancers are separately diagnosed risks. Supplied skin and brain frequencies are inconsistent with typical Lynch syndrome.
Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy directly damages skeletal muscle; intellectual disability and language delay occur in 2/3 reported patients.
Inherited rod-cone retinal degeneration with retinal pigment epithelial atrophy and visual field loss.
Immune-mediated rheumatic injury of the mitral valve defines the disease.
Diabetic metabolic disease with advanced retinal microvascular injury and pathological neovascularization; no other organ damage is inherent to this concept.
Hepatic and renal fibrotic disease define the syndrome; cardiac degeneration is a named defining component despite hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in only 3/15 patients.
Nonsyndromic intellectual disability with microcephaly and developmental delay; carbohydrate-transport ancestry alone does not establish a systemic metabolic disorder.
Hypothalamic TRH secretory deficiency causes central hypothyroidism; no separate structural neurologic injury is established.
Immune-mediated giant-cell inflammation directly destroys myocardium, causing arrhythmias and heart failure.
Adenocarcinoma originates in the ureter, which belongs to the renal axis.
Malignant cells directly infiltrate leptomeninges and the subarachnoid space; variable primary cancer sites are separate diseases.
Neuronopathic storage disease; splenic/marrow disease and cytopenias affect >30%, destructive bone disease 80-99%. Hepatic storage omitted by cap; gaze palsy is neurologic.
Anemia is the defining blood abnormality; the underlying chronic disease varies and does not justify another axis.
Skeletal dysplasia, microcephaly and abnormal dentition define disease; insulin resistance affects roughly 40-70%. Hearing loss (30-79%) omitted by cap; vascular risk excluded.
